EXHIBIT 99.1

Northstar Meridian to Acquire HarborCrate Logistics to Build Temperature-Controlled Distribution Platform

Combination Broadens Northstar Meridian’s Refrigerated Fulfillment Network and Expands Access to High-Growth Food, Pharmaceutical and Specialty-Chemical Supply Chains

HarborCrate Chief Executive Officer Maren Voss and Northstar Meridian Chief Executive Officer Elias Rourke

BOSTON, Apr. 18, 2027 7:00 a.m. EDT | ROTTERDAM, Apr. 18, 2027 1:00 p.m. CEST — Northstar Meridian Holdings plc (“Northstar Meridian,” NYSE: NMD) and HarborCrate Logistics, Ltd. (“HarborCrate,” Nasdaq: HCRL), an operator of temperature-controlled warehousing and last-mile distribution facilities, today announced that they have entered into a definitive agreement under which a subsidiary of Northstar Meridian will acquire all outstanding shares of HarborCrate’s common stock for $14.75 per share in cash, representing a premium of approximately 29% to HarborCrate’s closing price on April 17, 2027, a premium of approximately 43% to its volume-weighted average price over the preceding twelve months and a premium of approximately 61% to its volume-weighted average price over the preceding six months. The transaction values HarborCrate at approximately $612 million. The acquisition will give Northstar Meridian an expanded network of refrigerated fulfillment centers, cross-border transport capabilities and automated inventory systems serving food producers, specialty pharmacies and temperature-sensitive industrial customers. Demand for reliable cold-chain infrastructure is increasing as manufacturers and retailers seek more resilient distribution routes, tighter product traceability and reduced spoilage. HarborCrate’s facilities use sensor-based monitoring, modular freezer capacity and route-optimization software to support shipments requiring controlled temperature ranges. Northstar Meridian expects to integrate those capabilities with its existing freight brokerage and regional warehouse operations, creating a broader platform for time-sensitive products. The companies believe the combined network will improve asset utilization, shorten delivery windows and support customers that require auditable handling from production through final delivery. “HarborCrate has built a disciplined operating model around complex temperature-controlled logistics,” said Elias Rourke, Chief Executive Officer of Northstar Meridian. “Its facilities, monitoring systems and experienced teams will strengthen our ability to serve customers whose products cannot tolerate ordinary distribution conditions.”
